items.author: Guillermo Rauch
items.bio: @vercel CEO
items.summary_en:
Super bullish on WebMCP. Much like Tesla FSD meets the world where it is (streets, stoplights, potholes and all), agents *need* to ride the existing WWW infrastructure… WebMCP makes it more efficient.

Some pretty unique wins too. e.g: Next.js dev pages could expose debugging tools directly to agents in the specific tab they’re testing, with page-specific context, instead of sifting through server logs. No separate MCP server to find and configure because the page directly exposes its own 'agent tools'.

e.g: in this world 𝚏𝚡 + 𝚊𝚐𝚎𝚗𝚝-𝚋𝚛𝚘𝚠𝚜𝚎𝚛 is a complete web dev stack with zero loss in debugging depth
items.summary_zh: WebMCP 的关键价值是让 agents 直接骑在现有 WWW 基础设施上，而不是另起一套要找、要配的 MCP server。最锋利的场景是前端调试：Next.js 页面自己暴露带上下文的 agent tools，`fx + agent-browser` 就能成为零调试深度损失的完整 Web 开发栈。

items.bio: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
items.summary_en:
Here’s one practical thing you can do this weekend to get better at building AI products.

Pick a workflow you know well - from your personal life or your work.

Automate the whole thing with AI.

Use the AI product you’re comfortable with - you’ll probably have to experiment with a few.

This exercise will force you to think about

1/ What does a great end-to-end experience look like?
2/ How should you use MCPs and tools?
3/ Where should humans stay in the loop?
4/ How do you evaluate it?

Then keep expanding the ambition.

You’ll learn more by doing this once than by reading about AI product building for a month.

The only way to learn is to build.
items.summary_zh: 这个周末别再读 AI 产品方法论了，挑一个你最熟的工作流，用 AI 从头到尾自动化一遍。你会被迫搞清楚端到端体验、工具/MCP、人类介入和评估怎么设计；做一次，比读一个月都管用。

items.author: No Priors
items.title: Redefining Chip Architecture with Arm CEO Rene Haas
items.summary_en:
Speaker 1 | 00:00 - 00:15
There's no computing problem that's ever been invented that doesn't utilize and can't utilize the microprocessor. It is the heart of everything. All roads lead through it, around it, past it. Something has to do the orchestration, arbitration decision around where those tokens go. That's what CPUs do.

Speaker 1 | 00:15 - 00:36
Chip design can take anywhere from twenty four to thirty six months depending on the complexity of the chip, etcetera, etcetera. The actual design is not the largest amount of time. The largest amount of time is in the verification, the validation, the debug. AI is really good at that. And if we were to shut it off, it's like being in the 1990s, you've got internet and you're now saying, you know, only internet between the hours of two and four.

Speaker 2 | 00:36 - 00:37
Yeah.

Speaker 1 | 00:37 - 00:42
After that, go to the library that we have down the hall. It'd be anarchy. Yeah. The genie's out of the bottle and there's no stopping that.

Speaker 2 | 00:49 - 01:13
Hi, listeners. Welcome back to No Priors. Today, Elad and I are here with Renee Haas, the CEO of ARM and SoftBank Group International. We talk about the position of ARM within the chip industry, the resurgence of interest in chip innovation, the challenges of the supply chain, the future of robotics, energy, his place in the SoftBank Group, and how he sees workloads changing in the future and for ARM. Renee, thanks so much for doing this with us.

Speaker 1 | 01:13 - 01:13
Pleasure.

Speaker 2 | 01:14 - 01:36
Congratulations on the chip presentation at hot chips and, you know, all of the progress that ARM has made. I think there's enormous amount of interest from the technology industry and the software industry and just sort better understanding the chip
items.summary_zh: 微处理器是所有计算的心脏，最终都要靠 CPU 来编排、仲裁 token 往哪走。芯片设计最耗时的不是设计，而是验证、调试和排错；AI 已经把这块改写了，现在关掉它就像把互联网限时开放，混乱不可避免。
